scope: Composition guidance only. Manuscripts remain authoritative for models, edges and results. The five PDF-reread examples were approved for the project showcase on 2026-09-20; they are not new award references or independently validated results.

sivia_reference.method: Read paired prompts and inspect actual figures. Select principles, not whole layouts. Original Sivia image/prompt files are not redistributed here.

cases.borrow: Persistent identity across a local before/after change; allocate most area to the actual gate.
cases.exclude: Language-model mechanisms, benchmark metrics and repeated boxed panels.

cases.borrow: Observed state, candidate action and updated state remain visibly the same entity across time.
cases.exclude: Reinforcement-learning algorithms, invented probabilities and decorative process cards.

cases.borrow: Show the evidence carrier and the transformation, not a generic icon for each step.
cases.exclude: Multimodal-agent architecture, weak endpoint routing and unsupported performance chips.

global_review: Hide headings: can the scientific object and transformation still be recognized?
Each enclosure must denote a real boundary, matrix, coordinate domain or meaningful grouping; a method name alone is insufficient.
Can two unrelated paper examples swap layouts unchanged? If yes, redesign around the paper's actual relation.
Name the operand at both ends of each arrow. Prefer an explicit local source label over a tangled global route.
Use one dominant transformation with asymmetric support. More prompt detail must not become more in-figure prose.
Prompt length is a completeness gate, not proof of correctness or visual quality.

A.name: Physical mechanism / state evolution
A.use_when: The manuscript centers on a physical, biological or dynamical mechanism.
carriers: Signed interaction graph with named state variables
A.layout: A continuous mechanism or feedback loop; place validation beside the state it tests.
avoid: Generic nature clip art replacing state changes

B.name: Spatial decisions / iterative search
B.use_when: The manuscript couples location, resources and an iterative decision.
carriers: Actual resource location and next search region
B.layout: Use geography as the common coordinate frame; add local refinement and a state-update return.
avoid: Independent map thumbnails with inconsistent coordinates
An arrow to a title rather than an updated belief
checks: Does observation update the same spatial state?
Are feasible actions and resource limits visible?

C.name: Evidence / inference / matched comparison
C.use_when: Observed records constrain a latent variable or support comparisons.
carriers: Matched identities before and after an operator
C.layout: Make inference or the distinguishing operator dominant; route parallel analyses independently.
avoid: A chain that serializes independent analyses
Inferred quantities drawn as directly observed measurements
checks: Which conditional branch has zero change?

D.name: State / capacity / accounting / decision
D.use_when: The manuscript links operational state to economics and constrained actions.
carriers: Current state and forward decision time
D.layout: Integrate the physical limit with a ledger and a compact rolling state update; no five-card business pipeline.
avoid: Generic business icons instead of arithmetic
checks: Can the decision use only information available at that time?

E.name: Interactions / environmental transitions
E.use_when: The manuscript centers on ecological relations or interventions.
carriers: One environment changing under an intervention
E.layout: A food web, landscape transition or feedback mechanism with secondary scenario comparison.
avoid: Confusing scenario assumptions with observed results
checks: Are energy, biomass and control arrows distinguished?

F.name: Evidence / policy contrast / interpretation
F.use_when: The manuscript compares policies, populations or social outcomes.
carriers: Text spans mapped to policy themes
F.layout: Make the evidence structure and actual comparison dominant; descriptive grouping remains a smaller branch.
checks: Are policy groups distinct from descriptive clusters?
What is differenced and what is held comparable?
Are claims limited by measurement and source consistency?

a-typed-ecological-relations.critique: A generic ecological overview hid the sign and population-level meaning of the resource feedback.
a-typed-ecological-relations.replacement: Shared resource and host-parasite relations feed a decreasing male-fraction response and recruitment loop; compare sex-ratio settings separately.
scientific_guards: Eq.12 and its prose imply a decreasing male fraction as resources rise; Fig.7's conflicting positive sign is not copied.
Resource per individual is lambda/(N + sum Ni), not lambda/N.
k(1-m)^1.25 is a recruitment factor with a host-dependent term, not the complete population update.
Population/cohort sex composition is not individual adult sex change.
The ESI uses standardized resources and surviving species, not lamprey abundance as an additional operand.

b-rescue-multiscale-overview.critique: A generic search pipeline did not preserve the identity of the searched cells across the update.
b-rescue-multiscale-overview.replacement: A drift cross-section and two matched 7-by-7 maps show prior, no detection, exclusion, drift and redeployment.
scientific_guards: The Manhattan-distance Poisson-shell prior is assumed, not a calibrated posterior derived from Monte Carlo trajectories.
Excluding searched cells assumes perfect detection and no re-entry; show this limitation.
Eq.18 repeats a force component; Eqs.30/35 and the normalization prose conflict. Do not silently repair or certify these formulas.
Keep old excluded cells and the chosen cell at the same coordinates in both maps.
Summed probabilities over independent targets represent an expected count, not the probability of finding any target.

c-infer-compare-redesign.critique: Previous redesign split inference, rules, traits and MARS into repeated framed modules; few objects explained the actual operations.
c-infer-compare-redesign.replacement: Feasible share simplex → shared rule-conditional shares → two parallel analyses; enlarge rank rails and the AND-gated subtraction.
scientific_guards: Fan shares are relative, not measured totals.
Feasible-set and likelihood estimators have separate raw-data inputs.
Observed judges feed Judge outcome; inferred shares feed Inferred fan outcome.
Judge elite AND worse fan rank; otherwise S = S0; eliminate argmax S.
Weekly counterfactuals, not a full-season replay; keep tune/test seasons separate.
Fig.4's rank-sum argmin conflicts with rank 1 being best; follow the larger-risk/argmax convention in section 7.2.
Both outcome models have fixed plus random effects. Inferred-share uncertainty is not fully propagated into these fits.

d-wins-to-value-chain.critique: Five equal business cards and stock icons hid capacity censoring, accounting and the decision state.
d-wins-to-value-chain.replacement: Censored-demand density, explicit revenue and cash/debt identities, named action increments and a rolling state transition replace decorative arena and business cards.
scientific_guards: Expected attendance is E[min(d,K)|x], not min(E[d],K). Estimated demand covariates do not include fitted price elasticity; pricing response is an assumption.
Revenue sums streams; profit subtracts costs; cash is a separate state.

Section 7.2 states weighted Revenue/EBITDA/DCF aggregation without weights; later scenarios use revenue multiples and section 11 defers other methods. Preserve this source inconsistency; invent neither weights nor a blanket ban on aggregation.
Financing updates cash and debt; the source's simplified cash book adds profit, not a fully specified operating-cash-flow model.
Market-size scenarios scale other revenue; do not add an unsupported market-to-popularity or demand edge.
Joint roster/leverage choices use known state. Pricing remains a separate layer; injury is an exogenous scenario, not a validated stochastic process.

f-cyber-policy-evidence-map.critique: Three equal method panels replaced evidence with repeated icons and hid the comparison actually made.
f-cyber-policy-evidence-map.replacement: Country × year ledger, selected clustering columns, document themes, symbolic treated/control contrast and a smaller association branch.
scientific_guards: K-means uses NCSI and Legal Measures only.
Descriptive clusters are not policy treatment groups; distinguish them by color and labels.
DID subtracts the control change from the treated change; no invented effects or signs.
LDA describes topics; MIC/regression associations do not establish causation.
Source sign interpretations and significance statements conflict; depict symbolic contrasts, not a claimed empirical benefit.
MIC and factor analysis are parallel association analyses; the factor subset excludes GDP. Clustering K-selection prose also conflicts with its figure.
Underreporting and comparison-group limitations are not removed by the source's noise sensitivity analysis.
